entries.originalText: We cannot place too little confidence in ourselves, because grace and understanding are often lacking to us.
entries.modernizedText: We cannot place too little confidence in ourselves, because grace and understanding are often lacking in us.

entries.originalText: Little light is there within us, and what we have we quickly lose by negligence.
entries.modernizedText: There is little light within us, and what we have we quickly lose through negligence.

entries.originalText: Oftentimes we perceive not how great is our inward blindness.
entries.modernizedText: Often we do not perceive how great our inward blindness is.

entries.originalText: We often do ill and excuse it worse.
entries.modernizedText: We often do wrong and excuse it even worse.

entries.originalText: Sometimes we are moved by passion and count it zeal; we blame little faults in others and pass over great faults in ourselves.
entries.modernizedText: Sometimes we are moved by passion and call it zeal; we blame small faults in others and pass over great faults in ourselves.

entries.originalText: Quickly enough we feel and reckon up what we bear at the hands of others, but we reflect not how much others are bearing from us.
entries.modernizedText: We quickly feel and count up what we bear at the hands of others, but do not reflect on how much others are bearing from us.

entries.originalText: He who would weigh well and rightly his own doings would not be the man to judge severely of another.
entries.modernizedText: The person who weighs his own doings well and rightly would not judge another severely.

entries.originalText: The spiritually-minded man putteth care of himself before all cares; and he who diligently attendeth to himself easily keepeth silence concerning others.
entries.modernizedText: The spiritually minded person puts care of himself before all other cares; and the person who diligently attends to himself easily keeps silence about others.

entries.originalText: Thou wilt never be spiritually minded and godly unless thou art silent concerning other men’s matters and take full heed to thyself.
entries.modernizedText: You will never be spiritually minded and godly unless you are silent about other people’s affairs and pay full attention to yourself.

entries.originalText: If thou think wholly upon thyself and upon God, what thou seest out of doors shall move thee little.
entries.modernizedText: If you think wholly about yourself and God, what you see outside will move you little.

entries.originalText: Where art thou when thou art not present to thyself? and when thou hast overrun all things, what hath it profited thee, thyself being neglected?
entries.modernizedText: Where are you when you are not present to yourself? And when you have run through all things, what has it profited you, if you have neglected yourself?

entries.originalText: If thou wouldst have peace and true unity, thou must put aside all other things, and gaze only upon thyself.
entries.modernizedText: If you want peace and true unity, you must put aside all other things and gaze only upon yourself.

entries.originalText: Then thou shalt make great progress if thou keep thyself free from all temporal care.
entries.modernizedText: Then you will make great progress if you keep yourself free from all temporal care.

entries.originalText: Thou shalt lamentably fall away if thou set a value upon any worldly thing.
entries.modernizedText: You will fall away lamentably if you set value on any worldly thing.

entries.originalText: Let nothing be great, nothing high, nothing pleasing, nothing acceptable unto thee, save God Himself or the things of God.
entries.modernizedText: Let nothing be great, nothing high, nothing pleasing, nothing acceptable to you except God Himself or the things of God.

entries.originalText: Reckon as altogether vain whatsoever consolation comes to thee from a creature.
entries.modernizedText: Count as altogether vain whatever consolation comes to you from a creature.

entries.originalText: The soul that loveth God looketh not to anything that is beneath God.
entries.modernizedText: The soul that loves God looks to nothing beneath God.

entries.originalText: God alone is eternal and incomprehensible, filling all things, the solace of the soul, and the true joy of the heart.
entries.modernizedText: God alone is eternal and incomprehensible, filling all things, the solace of the soul and the true joy of the heart.
